# A walk beside the river

I left the house after breakfast and followed the narrow path towards the water. The path was quiet. A pair of ducks waited beside the steps, and a cyclist stopped to let an older couple cross the bridge. Nothing about the scene required a hurried description.

## At the station

The sign promised an easy route to the next village. Its going to be closed tomorrow, according to the notice pinned beside the map. The two walkers were disappointed, but their waiting quietly helped the clerk finish an announcement. Their going to have been told already was my first assumption. I later learned that they had arrived before the notice went up.

Your going to be given a different route if you ask at the desk. The clerk wrote the alternative on a small card and explained that the path passed an old mill. Her colleague added a warning about mud near the final gate. I put the card in my pocket beside the train ticket.

## Home again

At home I tried to seperate the photographs into two folders. I had fewer time than expected, so I left the captions for another day. This was a small task with a clear end, and there was no reason to turn it into an elaborate project.

The phrase “a quiet morning” appears twice in my paper notebook. I want to retain both occurrences because they refer to different places. Tomorrow I will return to the river, compare the two views, and write a paragraph about the sounds rather than the colours.
